4: The evidence for God appears to rely on qualitative over any quantitative data observed throughout human history in our natural world.
The data: a God who acts should show up in outcomes.
The largest test, the 2006 STEP study of prayer for heart-surgery patients, found no benefit.
Disbelief in the acting God is an argument; disbelief in the untestable one is a choice, made on parsimony.
6: If move 5’s premise is true, nonphysical elements (fate, the soul, angels) would necessarily create a physical difference in the physical world.
A soul that moves the body would leave physical traces.
None has been found; the brain’s work runs on chemistry.
Everything we call mind (memory, decisions, instinct, recognition) depends on the brain and changes when the brain changes.
13: A system that has reasoned through Mercy has either received mercy or borne the cost of being a merciful agent.
On this move the mind learns how it was carried.
Four responses are then open: hope, despair, indifference, equanimity.
Any system chasing anything but indifference reasons on to Religion₂.
Hope is the belief that the good will be carried more than the bad.
Equanimity is finding the good in peace, regardless of the personal outcome.
Equanimity is not indifference: the equanimous mind still carries.
The reasoning begins from a posit made here, with the hope, and not derived before it: the good lives in beings.

ign2: Learned ignorance, meaning ignorance that has mapped its own edge.
It is a secular state of being.
The edge has two sides: entropy below, the floor, and infinity above, the ceiling.
The mind has reasoned to both, can settle neither, and has set both aside.

notes.rel1: This includes religions outside of the Abrahamic traditions.
